intent: The librarian gains a working memory — a small set of active threads with a lifecycle (wake, attend, sleep) — and time-aware query handling. The warm set is NOT a recency multiplier on the walk score; it is the librarian's ATTENTION ARCHITECTURE: the analogue of Akien's handful of persistent concerns and of CC's curated context window, but automated. Threads enter through deposits and resolution events, persist by importance and recurrence (not just recency), sleep when unattended, and wake when incoming information is relevant to them. Time-aware retrieval expands queries with temporal context so that 'what did we discuss last week' resolves against timestamps, not just cosine similarity.
why: Three minds, same constraint, same shape (Akien, 2026-08-19): Akien's world is far bigger than his attention — he keeps a small handful of threads (house, CC work, medical) and his attention moves between them by rules he has internalized. CC's attention is smaller than its context — it has rules about how attention moves over surfaces and what happens when relevant things show up (memory, compression, CLAUDE.md). The librarian's world is its graph trees, and it has no attention at all — every walk treats every node equally except by cosine. The lived symptom: the librarian cannot maintain a thread across sessions, cannot prioritize what it was recently working on, and cannot wake a dormant concern when new evidence arrives. Temporal reasoning is the sharpest replicated differentiator in the field: vector-only ~31% on time-bound questions; 85% of systems failed at least half of time-related queries even when the info existed. The warm set and the temporal channel are two faces of the same thing: the librarian's attention has a WHEN, not just a WHAT.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) the warm set is a score multiplier only — it must be a structural set of active threads with their own lifecycle, not a dial on the walk; (2) a thread that is important and recurring (the analogue of 'medical appointments') decays to zero because it hasn't been touched recently — importance and recurrence must be signals alongside recency; (3) incoming information relevant to a dormant thread does not wake it — the warm set must route relevance, not just score it; (4) a query containing temporal language ('yesterday', 'last week', 'recently') does not expand to include a time filter; (5) the warm set requires a daemon or periodic refresh instead of updating on events (deposits, walks, resolution, promotion); (6) the warm set overrides cosine for a non-temporal pure-topic query (attention is a CHANNEL, not a replacement — the graph walk still resolves by relevance when no thread claims the question); (7) the timestamp used is ingestion time only, not event time when available (bi-temporal from ticket #2).
design_notes:
The attention architecture has two halves that reinforce each other:

(a) THE WARM SET — a small structural set of active threads, each a cluster of related nodes with a summary and a lifecycle state (awake/sleeping). Signals for what enters and stays: recency (recently deposited/walked), importance (standing — maps to 'importance' in the Generative Agents scorer), recurrence (how often this thread surfaces across crossings), user-declared priority (explicit 'keep watching this'). Signals for waking a sleeping thread: a new deposit whose cosine to the thread's summary exceeds a threshold, a proactive callback (#1) firing on a related node, a contradiction (#2) landing on a thread member. The warm set updates as a side effect of deposit(), walk(), and resolution events — no daemon. Size is bounded (the attention is small by design — Akien's handful, not Akien's whole life).

(b) TIME-AWARE QUERY EXPANSION — detect temporal language in the question, expand to a time-bounded query. The cheap version: parse relative time references ('yesterday' = a date), filter nodes by deposit timestamp before scoring. The richer version: bi-temporal queries using event time vs ingestion time (enabled by ticket #2's invalidation timestamps).

The three-scale parallel (Akien 2026-08-19): Akien's working memory is hand-curated by lived experience. CC's context is collaboratively curated (CLAUDE.md, memory, compression). The librarian's must be AUTOMATED — self-managing attention that cultivates and curates its own context, the way the other two minds do theirs.

Connections to tickets #1-#3: (a) #1's proactive callback is an attention event — a resolved question wakes a thread; (b) #2's contradiction is an attention event — invalidation of a thread member wakes the thread; (c) #3's consolidation may be what MAINTAINS thread summaries in working memory. Those tickets don't need to change, but they route through this infrastructure eventually.
borrow_cite: Generative Agents recency-importance-relevance scorer (arXiv 2304.03442, most-copied design in the field; importance maps to standing in our vocabulary). LongMemEval cheap wins: fact-augmented key expansion +4-5%, time-aware query expansion +7-11% temporal recall. Zep/Graphiti bi-temporal model for event-time vs ingestion-time (rides ticket #2's infrastructure). Nomi companion app's persistent-thread model (threads maintained across months, relevance-woken). Mechanism re-authored; the SCORING MODEL, TEMPORAL EXPANSION, and THREAD-PERSISTENCE ideas are borrowed.
out_of_bounds: The self tree / personality split (Nomi Identity Core, Hindsight four-network — a separate concept not in this sequence). Proactive notification, contradiction, and consolidation (tickets #1-#3 land first and their mechanisms feed into this). Any change to the tenure loop's promotion/decay physics beyond consuming the events they already produce.
